description: A six headed sample player. One sample is loaded at a time and each of the six playheads plays its own selection out of it, with its own speed, pitch, volume, pan and stereo output

params.text: Sets that playhead's speed, -2x to +2x; a negative speed plays its selection backwards
How much of the speed input reaches that playhead's speed
Shifts that playhead in octaves
A tap switches that playhead on and off
Switched on, that playhead's selection repeats
A tap starts that playhead from the beginning of its selection
A tap stops that playhead where it is, and the next one carries on from there
Switched on, that playhead plays only while a gate is high at its start input
Sets where in the sample that playhead's selection starts
Sets where in the sample that playhead's selection ends
How much of the volume input reaches that playhead's volume
Sets that playhead's volume
Places that playhead in the stereo field
Stretches the wave display vertically, and changes nothing about the sound
Sets a fade at the start and the end of playback to keep clicks out; it also sets the crossfade between the start of the sample and its reversed end, up to 1 second
A tap stores the settings of all six playheads as a new keyframe
A tap loads the current keyframe, setting all six playheads from it
A tap replaces the current keyframe with the settings the six playheads have now
A tap deletes the current keyframe
A tap goes to the first keyframe
A tap steps back to the previous keyframe
A tap steps on to the next keyframe
A tap picks a keyframe at random
Picks which keyframe is the current one
Sets the volume of the mix at the total outputs
Sets a speed applied to all six playheads
How much of the global speed input reaches the speed of all six playheads
A tap picks the next sample in the list
A tap picks the previous sample in the list

inputs.text: A voltage moving that playhead's speed
A pitch voltage at 1V per octave, which plays that playhead's selection chromatically
A pulse starts that playhead from the beginning of its selection, and with its gated flag on a gate holds it
A pulse stops that playhead where it is, and the next one carries on from there
A pulse switches that playhead on and off
A voltage moving the start of that playhead's selection
A voltage moving the end of that playhead's selection
A voltage moving that playhead's volume
A pulse stores the settings of all six playheads as a new keyframe
A pulse loads the current keyframe, setting all six playheads from it
A pulse replaces the current keyframe with the settings the six playheads have now
A pulse deletes the current keyframe
A pulse goes to the first keyframe
A pulse steps back to the previous keyframe
A pulse steps on to the next keyframe
A pulse picks a keyframe at random
A voltage picks which keyframe is the current one
A voltage moving the speed of all six playheads
A voltage picks the sample from the list, read as a note: 0V, which is C3, is the first sample in the list, C sharp the second, and so on
A pulse picks the next sample in the list
A pulse picks the previous sample in the list

outputs.text: One side of that playhead's own stereo output; patching it takes that playhead out of the mix carried by the total outputs
A pulse each time that playhead reaches the end of its selection
One side of the stereo mix of every playhead whose own outputs are unpatched

notes: dragging a playhead with the alt key held moves it with granular playback; with the left shift key held it scratches that playhead, and with the right shift key held, every playhead at once
nothing sounds until a sample is loaded; drop an audio file onto the module or load one from the menu
every playable audio file in the folder the loaded sample came from is listed, and that list is what the sample select controls step through
menu: Output 0V when stopped — holds the outputs at 0V while a playhead is stopped or paused, rather than holding the last voltage
Don't reset playhead on keyframe change (if possible) — leaves the playheads where they are when a keyframe changes, instead of resetting them
Open WAV or AIFF File... — loads a wav or aiff file as the sample
